title: The branch does not strain
body: A branch bears fruit by staying joined to the vine, not by trying harder. Jesus puts the weight on remaining in him; the fruit follows from the connection. Cut off, the most gifted branch produces nothing.

title: Pruning is not punishment
body: The vinedresser cuts back the branches that are already bearing so they bear more. A season of loss can be the Father making room, not turning away.

title: Joy is the stated purpose
body: Jesus says he taught about abiding so that his own joy would be in his friends and their joy would be complete. Obedience is the road, and joy is where it is meant to lead.

title: Seek first, then the rest
body: Food, clothes and tomorrow are real needs, and the Father knows them. Put his kingdom first and let each day carry only its own trouble.

title: A lighter yoke
body: The invitation is to the tired and the overloaded. Rest comes from taking on his yoke and learning from him, because he is gentle and what he asks fits.

title: Restless until
body: Augustine opens his confession with the observation that people are made for God and stay unsettled until they find their rest in him. Much ambition is that restlessness looking for a home.

title: God among the pots and pans
body: Brother Lawrence worked in a monastery kitchen and treated every small task as a conversation with God. He found the noise of the kitchen no further from God than the hour of prayer.
source: Brother Lawrence, The Practice of the Presence of God

title: New every morning
body: Written in the ruins of Jerusalem: the Lord's mercies have not run out, and a fresh supply arrives each morning. Yesterday's failure does not use up today's portion.

title: Planted by the water
body: The person who turns God's instruction over day and night is like a tree set beside a stream. It gives fruit when the season comes and its leaves stay green through the dry months.

title: Renewed, not pressed into shape
body: The world presses everyone into its mould. The alternative Paul gives is change from the inside, through a mind that is being made new, so you can recognise what God wants.

title: Guard the spring
body: Everything you do flows out of the heart, so that is the thing to watch most closely. What you let in and dwell on becomes the water everyone else drinks.

title: A city without walls
body: A person who cannot govern their own spirit is like a city whose walls are broken through. Anything that wants to can walk in.

title: Better than taking a city
body: Being slow to anger outranks military strength, and ruling your own spirit outranks conquering a city. The harder victory is the inner one.

title: Run to win
body: Every athlete in training goes without things for a wreath that withers. Paul trains with the same seriousness for a prize that lasts, and keeps his body under command so he does not disqualify himself.

title: Consider the ant
body: The ant has no overseer and still stores food in summer. Nobody is coming to make you prepare; the wise do it without being told.

title: Getting out of bed
body: When you do not want to get up, Marcus Aurelius suggests telling yourself that you are rising to do the work of a human being. You were not made to stay warm under the blankets.

title: Thirteen virtues, one at a time
body: Franklin listed thirteen virtues and gave each one a full week of attention, marking his failures in a small book. Working on everything at once had got him nowhere; one at a time, the marks thinned out.

title: Faithful in little
body: Whoever can be trusted with very little can be trusted with much. Character does not change size with the stakes, so the small unseen task is the real test.

title: Do not grow weary
body: Doing good is tiring and the harvest is slow. Paul's promise is that it comes at the proper time for those who do not give up.

title: Hearing is not doing
body: Listening to the word without acting on it is like glancing in a mirror and forgetting your own face. The blessing is attached to the doing.

title: What is yours to control
body: Some things are up to us: our judgments, aims and choices. Everything else, including reputation, health and other people, is not. Epictetus says peace begins with keeping the two lists apart.

title: The judgment, not the event
body: People are disturbed less by what happens than by their opinion about what happens. Change the opinion and the same event loses most of its force.

title: We suffer more in imagination
body: Seneca tells his friend that more things frighten us than actually hurt us. Much of what we dread never arrives, and we pay for it in advance anyway.

title: A retreat you carry with you
body: People look for quiet in the country, by the sea or in the hills. Marcus Aurelius notes you can withdraw into your own mind at any hour, and nowhere is quieter if it is well ordered.

title: Be still
body: In a psalm full of shaking mountains and raging nations, the command is to stop and know that he is God. Stillness here is an act of trust in the middle of the noise.

title: Prayer in place of worry
body: Paul's instruction is to turn every anxiety into a request, with thanks. What follows is a peace that goes beyond understanding and stands guard over heart and mind.

title: Choose what you think about
body: Whatever is true, honourable, just, pure, lovely and worth praising: Paul says to keep your mind on these. Attention is a decision, and it shapes the person.

title: Contentment is learned
body: Paul says he learned to be content with plenty and with hunger alike. It did not come naturally; it came through Christ, who gave him strength for both.

title: Quick to listen
body: Be fast to hear, slow to speak and slow to get angry. Most regretted sentences were said in the wrong order.

title: As for the Lord
body: Whatever the task, do it wholeheartedly, as work done for the Lord and not for a boss. The audience changes the quality of the work.

title: With all your might
body: Whatever your hand finds to do, put your strength into it. The Teacher's reason is blunt: there is no working or planning in the grave you are heading toward.

title: Stay with a few authors
body: Seneca warns that reading many books in passing is like a traveller with many hosts and no friends. Linger with a limited number of great minds, and take one thing each day to digest.

title: Life is long enough
body: We are not given a short life, Seneca argues; we make it short by wasting most of it. Spent well, it is long enough for the highest things.
source: Seneca, On the Shortness of Life

title: The morning question
body: Franklin began each day's plan with a question: what good shall I do today? He ended it with another: what good have I done?

title: Iron sharpens iron
body: One person sharpens another the way iron sharpens iron. Friction with a good friend makes both of you more useful.

title: Built on rock
body: Two builders hear the same words and face the same storm. The house that stands belongs to the one who put the words into practice.

title: Number your days
body: Moses asks God to teach us to count our days so that we gain a wise heart. Knowing the supply is limited changes how you spend it.

title: What is required
body: Micah reduces it to three things: do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with your God.

title: The obstacle becomes the way
body: What stands in the path of action can be turned into the material for action. Marcus Aurelius treats the hindrance as the next thing to work with.

title: Stop arguing, be one
body: Do not spend more time debating what a good person is like. Be one.

title: The best revenge
body: The best way to answer someone who wrongs you is to not become like them.

title: Meeting difficult people
body: Tell yourself each morning that you will meet the meddling, the ungrateful and the arrogant. They act from ignorance of good and evil, and none of them can drag you into what is shameful.

title: Strong and courageous
body: As Joshua takes over from Moses, the command comes with its reason: do not be afraid, because the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.

title: Not a spirit of fear
body: What God gives is power, love and a sound mind. Timidity did not come from him.

title: Strength exchanged
body: Even the young grow tired and fall. Those who wait on the Lord trade their strength for his: they rise on wings like eagles, run without wearying and walk without fainting.

title: Lay it aside and run
body: With a crowd of witnesses around us, drop every weight and the sin that tangles your feet. Run the race set for you with endurance, eyes on Jesus, who starts and finishes faith.
